description: Merge vertices closer than a tolerance into one (Blender's Mesh > Merge by Distance / bmo_remove_doubles / weld modifier). Spatial-hash bucketing for O(n); rebuild faces on the merged vertex set; drop faces that collapse to a degenerate (<3 distinct verts) after welding. Hardens boolean output and imported polygon soups before the CSG/polyMesh export bridges. New MeshOp::Weld { tolerance } variant + dispatch. V&V: coincident-duplicated cube welds 16->8 verts back to chi=2; a slit sphere seam welds to watertight; tolerance=0 is a no-op.
title: outram-blender: weld / remove-doubles (merge coincident vertices within tolerance)

description:
FOUND AND FIXED 2026-09-04 while doing op-190j.4.

DynamicColumn::profiles computed interior-stage vapour flows as v[j] = rest / hv[j] — dividing by an ABSOLUTE molar enthalpy. Absolute enthalpies are defined only up to the reference state, so the answer depended on where the enthalpy scale is zeroed.

Benzene/toluene at ~360 K sits on the positive side of this crate's reference and worked, which is why op-6rhz's V&V never saw it. Heavy petroleum pseudo-components at CDU temperatures sit on the NEGATIVE side: hv = -914.8 J/mol at stage 10 of the reference crude column. Two symptoms followed:

  * check_latent(hv[j]) rejected the column outright ('energy-balance denominator -914.8 J/mol is non-physical'). That check is correct for the reboiler, whose divisor hv-hl IS a latent heat, and wrong for the interior stages, whose divisor is not.
  * With the check relaxed, the sweep returned a NEGATIVE vapour flow and hence a negative distillate (-0.228 mol/s), then diverged: inventory 1.6e3 -> 4.8e3 -> 1.9e19 -> 8.2e38 within 30 steps. Larger holdups only delayed it. Measured with AND without side draws, so side draws were not implicated.

FIX: rewrite the interior-stage balance in enthalpy DIFFERENCES relative to that stage's own liquid, which is the textbook form and the one the reboiler balance already used. Subtracting h^L_j x (stage mass balance) removes the reference; the divisor becomes the latent heat h^V_j - h^L_j, positive and order thousands of J/mol whatever the reference. Added check_enthalpy_divisor (finite, |.| > 1) for the stage-1 divisor, which mixes absolute terms and legitimately can be negative; check_latent keeps its original meaning at the reboiler.

EVIDENCE IT IS RIGHT:
  * The benzene V&V test (op-6rhz, distillation_sim_v1) still passes unchanged — the fix does not move the validated case.
  * The crude plant now holds its steady seed for 200+ steps at every inventory tried (tau 30/90/300 s, vessel 50/400/2000 mol), distillate 0.3376 mol/s in all of them. Independence from the inventory is the signature of the reference term being gone; before the fix the divergence rate tracked the holdup.
  * Regression test: crude_plant::tests::the_steady_answer_does_not_depend_on_the_inventory.

Related: op-190j.5 (the steady bubble-point defects), op-190j.4 (the crude sim this blocked).
title: columns/dynamic: interior-stage energy sweep was enthalpy-reference dependent

description:
Found 2026-09-12 while chasing op-mzvp.2.12 (ring-RPT +4004 pcm). Sibling of
op-i7u9 (the angular oracle, which excluded the angle).

WHAT IS WRONG. ThermalScattering's emission tables sit on a 48-point log grid
over 1e-5 .. 4 eV (material/thermal.rs, N_EMIT_GRID = 48), so ADJACENT INCIDENT
ENERGIES ARE 31.6 % APART, and select_table picks between the two bracketing
tables by ACE statistical interpolation. Mixing two tables whose means are
31.6 % apart adds a variance r(1-r)(m2-m1)^2 that the true kernel has not got.
Above ~0.4 eV, where the kernel's own relative width has fallen to w ~ 0.12,
that added variance DOMINATES.

MEASURED vs NJOY2016 THERMR MF=6/MT=229 (second moment, 600 K, quadrature on the
oracle side, 400k samples on ours):

  E [eV]   w NJOY   w ours   rel        w ours (N_EMIT_GRID=192)  rel
  0.0253   0.79241  0.71967   -9.18 %   0.72008                   -9.13 %
  0.05     0.54768  0.48432  -11.57 %   0.48322                  -11.77 %
  0.2      0.27905  0.26517   -4.98 %   0.25740                   -7.76 %
  0.39     0.22681  0.25083  +10.59 %   0.21578                   -4.86 %
  0.625    0.19328  0.21794  +12.76 %   0.18610                   -3.72 %
  2.02     0.13644  0.18971  +39.04 %   0.13329                   -2.31 %
  3.75     0.11994  0.16209  +35.15 %   0.11740                   -2.11 %

The SIGN FLIP at 0.39 eV is the tell: below it what is measured is the 16-bin
equiprobable representation truncating its own tails (one-signed narrow, which
is expected and is the residual after the fix); above it, the grid dominates.
Raising N_EMIT_GRID 48 -> 192 collapses +39.0 % to -2.3 %, which confirms the
cause is the grid and not the S(alpha,beta) integration.

NOTE this is INVISIBLE to every existing thermal gate: the cross section is the
AREA, <E'>/E is the MEAN (0.1 % above 0.2 eV), xi and the free-gas asymptote are
first moments, and the new mubar gate is the angle. Only the second moment sees
it.

WORTH, MEASURED NOT ASSUMED. examples/fhr_ring_rpt_endf.rs,
OUTRAM_RINGRPT_ONLY=csg, same deck and seed:
  N_EMIT_GRID = 48   k = 1.40745 +/- 0.00214   p(2-group) 0.5254
  N_EMIT_GRID = 192  k = 1.40682 +/- 0.00221   p(2-group) 0.5249
-63 pcm, inside its own sampling error. So it is NOT the +4004 pcm residual.

FIX. Raise N_EMIT_GRID (192 was measured; pick from a convergence study), or
interpolate the two bracketing emission tables' outgoing energies rather than
choosing one of them statistically. EITHER WAY IT IS A RE-BASELINING: it shifts
every recorded thermal k-eff by tens of pcm, so the recorded-keff gates
(fhr_ring_rpt, htr10, hst009, lct008, triso_*) must be re-measured in the same
pass. That is why it was left at 48 here.

GATED AS (characterisation, not a blessing):
vv::njoy_golden::GRAPHITE_KERNEL_WIDTH + _TOL (50 %, sized to catch it growing)
+ _NARROW_TOL (15 %, one-signed, below 0.2 eV),
examples/graphite_sab_angle_and_width_vs_njoy_thermr.rs,
tests/thermal_laws_vs_njoy_thermr.rs::graphite_sab_kernel_width_against_njoy_thermr.
TIGHTEN THE 50 % TO ~15 % WHEN FIXED. NEVER WIDEN.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content:
FIXED 2026-09-12. N_EMIT_GRID 48 -> 384 and N_OUTGOING 16 -> 64, both sized by a
sweep against the NJOY THERMR oracle rather than chosen
(examples/thermal_emission_grid_convergence.rs, new).

TWO defects, not one, in the two dimensions of the emission tabulation:

  * incident-energy grid (N_EMIT_GRID) -> the kernel too BROAD above 0.4 eV
    (+39.0 % at 2 eV), from the r(1-r)(m2-m1)^2 added by statistical table
    interpolation. Converges: worst/rms at 64 outgoing bins is -2.45/1.65 % at
    192, -2.50/1.78 % at 384, -2.56/1.81 % at 768, -2.59/1.85 % at 1536. 384 is
    where it stops improving; its residual distance from the converged
    1536-point answer is <= 0.6 points against 192's <= 1.5, and 192 still
    carries a one-signed BROAD bias (+0.17 % at 0.625 eV where converged is
    -1.32 %). 768 halves that residual for 1.7x the reconstruction time and no
    change in worst-case or rms agreement.

  * equiprobable outgoing bins (N_OUTGOING) -> the kernel too NARROW everywhere,
    one-signed, since a finite equiprobable set truncates both tails. Graphite
    worst width: -11.60 % at 16 bins, -5.96 % at 32, -2.50 % at 64, -1.65 % at
    128. No plateau (falls as ~1/n_out), so 64 is a cost cut, not convergence.
    Nearly free: +0.9 s reconstruction and NO change in sampling throughput
    (10.33 vs 10.56 Msample/s), only memory 432 kB -> 1.7 MB per scatterer.

RESULT vs NJOY (200k samples, gate's own): graphite kernel width is now
one-signed narrow at all 13 energies, worst -2.33 %, rms 1.78 %, against
+39.0 %/-11.6 % before. <E'>/E worst -0.56 % (was -1.53 %). mubar unchanged
within its own noise (-0.0084 worst, was +0.0085), as expected -- refining the
energy bins does not sharpen the angular law.

ALSO FIXED, same file: select_table and interp_linear scanned their grid
LINEARLY from index 0, i.e. O(n_emit) per thermal sample. Replaced by
partition_point (exact same bracket). Thermal sampling went 6.06 -> 11.22
Msample/s at 48 points, and the cost of the finer grid fell from -33 % to -8 %.
This is what makes 384 affordable.

#188 IS NOT THE SAME DEFECT -- measured, not assumed. H-in-H2O's kernel is
INSENSITIVE to N_EMIT_GRID (<E'>/E at 1.5 meV: -5.40 % at 48 points, -5.51 % at
1536) and responds only to N_OUTGOING (-5.51/-3.26/-2.10/-1.43 % at 16/32/64/128
bins). Same class -- the ACE equiprobable pre-tabulation -- different dimension.
op-77pu is MITIGATED, not closed: worst <E'>/E -5.54 % -> -1.63 %, but xi only
-3.24 % -> -2.89 % (and -2.79 % even at 128 bins). The proper fix is a
continuous outgoing-energy law (NJOY iform=1), not more bins.

TOLERANCES TIGHTENED (never widened): GRAPHITE_KERNEL_WIDTH_TOL 0.50 -> 0.04 and
now one-signed narrow over the WHOLE table (GRAPHITE_KERNEL_WIDTH_NARROW_TOL
0.15 -> 0.04, INTRINSIC_BELOW_EV 0.2 -> 4.0 eV); GRAPHITE_KERNEL_TOL 0.02 ->
0.01; GRAPHITE_KERNEL_CONVERGED_TOL 0.004 -> 0.002; H2O_KERNEL_TOL 0.06 -> 0.03.
New golden H2O_KERNEL_WIDTH + gate h2o_sab_kernel_width_against_njoy_thermr.

k IMPACT, FHR ring-RPT CSG pebble, same deck, same seed, 4000 x [30 + 80]:
  48x16  k = 1.40745 +/- 0.00214   (reproduces the previously recorded value)
  384x64 k = 1.40546 +/- 0.00234
  delta = -199 +/- 317 pcm, 0.63 sigma -- STILL NOT RESOLVED at that deck's own
  statistics, and recorded as such. See examples/thermal_kernel_keff_worth.rs.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content:
Independent confirmation that the emission-table resize was worth it, from an oracle it was not tuned against (op-bo02, gh:#191 -- the equilibrium fixed point of the kernel, not any per-collision moment). Same random walk, same statistics, only the constants differ:

  c_Graphite 600 K    48x16: T_eff 614.28 +/- 0.83 K, shape 1.5652 (-6.09 %)
                     384x64: T_eff 607.21 +/- 0.89 K, shape 1.6286 (-2.31 %)
  c_H_in_H2O 293.6 K  48x16: T_eff 291.14 +/- 0.22 K, shape 1.5806 (-5.17 %)
                     384x64: T_eff 294.48 +/- 0.24 K, shape 1.6309 (-2.11 %)

So -7.1 K of graphite's fixed-point displacement and two thirds of the shape deficit, and water's fixed point moved THROUGH its nominal temperature (2.5 K low -> 0.9 K high) while the shape repaired monotonically. A displacement that changes sign under refinement is a discretisation error, which is this bead's diagnosis.

What is LEFT after the resize is op-bo02: graphite still 1.24 % hot, both laws still ~2 % narrow.

k IMPACT, FHR ring-RPT CSG pebble, same deck, same seed, 4000 x [30 + 80]:
  48x16  k = 1.40745 +/- 0.00214   (reproduces the previously recorded value)
  384x64 k = 1.40546 +/- 0.00234
  delta = -199 +/- 317 pcm, 0.63 sigma -- STILL NOT RESOLVED at that deck's own
  statistics, and recorded as such. See examples/thermal_kernel_keff_worth.rs.

K-WORTH, RESOLVED 2026-09-12 on a graphite-moderated k_inf medium (C/HM = 400,
reflective cube, 600 K), 720 000 active histories per tabulation, same seeds --
examples/thermal_kernel_keff_worth.rs:

  48x16  (superseded)   k_inf = 1.38976 +/- 0.00138      --
  384x16 (grid only)    k_inf = 1.38351 +/- 0.00146   -624 +/- 201 pcm  3.1 sigma
  48x64  (bins only)    k_inf = 1.38737 +/- 0.00148   -239 +/- 203 pcm  1.2 sigma
  384x64 (current)      k_inf = 1.38605 +/- 0.00137   -371 +/- 194 pcm  1.9 sigma

The two dimensions are NOT additive -- -624 and -239 separately, -371 together --
which is what two errors pulling opposite ways on the width should do. Fixing
only the grid over-corrects; fixing only the bins under-corrects.

INDEPENDENT CONFIRMATION from op-bo02 / gh:#191 (another agent's fixed-point
oracle, which this resize was not tuned against), same walk, same statistics:
  graphite T_eff 614.28 K (+2.38 %) -> 607.21 K (+1.20 %), shape 1.5652 -> 1.6286
  H2O      T_eff 291.14 K (-0.84 %) -> 294.48 K (+0.30 %), shape 1.5806 -> 1.6308
  free-gas C-12 control 601.28 K in BOTH -- identical to the digit, so only the
  tabulation moved.
Residual: graphite still 1.20 % hot. Extrapolating the measured slope (52 pcm/K)
puts that at ~ -380 pcm on this medium and ~ -200 pcm on the FHR pebble if
removed -- right SIGN for the +4004 pcm ring-RPT residual (ours reads high; a hot
fixed point raises k) and about 5 % of its SIZE. Not the residual.

title: outram-mc: graphite S(a,b) emission grid is too coarse -- kernel WIDTH +39% at 2 eV from statistical table interpolation
